name: Dudo
summary: South American liar's dice bluffing game where players bid on total dice faces hidden under cups.
rules_text: Each player starts with 5 dice and a cup. Each round all players shake and conceal their dice, then look at only their own. In clockwise order starting from the loser of last round, players bid: a number and a face, claiming at least that many dice among all players show that face. Ones are wild and count as any face. A bid must increase either the quantity, the face value, or both. Bidding aces is special: to switch to aces you may halve the current quantity rounded up; to switch from aces you must more than double the quantity. Instead of raising, a player may call Dudo. All cups are lifted. If the bid is true (at least as many dice as claimed), the caller loses one die; otherwise the bidder loses one die. Losing your last die eliminates you. Last player with dice wins.
rating_reason: Liar's dice with hidden cups, bidding, bluffing classic.
